verification_scope: Independent reading of assessment, relevant response, and cited primary publication metadata; original code was not independently rerun.
original_title: Targeting High Ability Entrepreneurs Using Community Information: Mechanism Design in the Field
materiality_scope: Secondary comparison; central incremental-information claim survives.
error: Wrong ordering variable: code forms terciles from predicted profits when the outcome is income.
affected_claim: Community rankings outperform prediction from observable characteristics for the income outcome.
corrected_direction: Reverses the secondary comparison: observable characteristics predict better after correction.
evidence_locator: DP049 PDF pp. 6–7; corrected tables PDF pp. 12–14.
public_date_evidence: I4R series issue cover August 2023. Internal May 31 manuscript date is not established public availability.
cohort_recommendation: Include only if substantial secondary-claim errors qualify; do not characterize main conclusion as overturned.

verification_scope: Independent reading of assessment, relevant response, and cited primary publication metadata; original code was not independently rerun.
original_title: Measuring the Welfare Effects of Shame and Pride
materiality_scope: Secondary curvature statistic changes; material effect on central welfare conclusions is not established.
error: Treatment-order coding and standardized-curvature calculation errors.
affected_claim: Similarity of Prolific and YMCA curvature estimates; treatment-order coefficient.
corrected_direction: Prolific curvature rises from 0.245 to 0.394; central welfare calculations barely change.
evidence_locator: DP064 PDF pp. 6–8 and Appendix B, PDF p. 14.
public_date_evidence: I4R series issue cover September 2023; internal July 26 date is not a verified public posting.
cohort_recommendation: Exclude from strict consequential-central-error cohort. Retain in inventory as verified limited error.

verification_scope: Independent reading of assessment, relevant response, and cited primary publication metadata; original code was not independently rerun.
original_title: Public Infrastructure and Economic Development: Evidence from Postal Systems
materiality_scope: A stated robustness check fails after correction; main full-sample estimate is unchanged.
error: Code selects states having any stable-border county although the stated restriction requires all counties to have stable borders.
affected_claim: Postal infrastructure result is robust to restricting to states whose county borders do not change.
corrected_direction: Restricted-sample estimate attenuates toward zero and becomes imprecise.
cohort_recommendation: Secondary robustness-error stratum; do not describe main effect as refuted.

verification_scope: Independent reading of assessment, relevant response, and cited primary publication metadata; original code was not independently rerun.
original_title: Finance and Green Growth
materiality_scope: Formal correction confirms GMM endogenous-variable implementation error and smaller coefficient magnitudes; authors and editors retain primary conclusions.
error: GMM code omitted the option specifying endogenous variables; some inference descriptions also incorrectly reported country clustering.
affected_claim: GMM effect magnitudes and associated precision.
corrected_direction: Formal correction reports smaller magnitudes; a clean original-to-corrected numerical contrast is not independently established in this review.

replicator_gmm.warning: Includes an extra regressor lag disputed by original authors; not a pure coding-error correction contrast.

evidence_locator: DP095 PDF pp. 7–8 and Table 1 PDF p. 12; DP096 PDF pp. 5–7; formal correction.
public_date_evidence: DP095 and response DP096 were I4R December 2023 issues. November 2023 manuscript/readers-contact dates do not by themselves prove public disclosure.
cohort_recommendation: Verified substantive implementation error; use December 2023 rather than January 2025 as earliest verified event year. Do not attribute the replicators fourfold attenuation entirely to the error.
original_publication_evidence: Oxford article history explicitly states published October 27, 2022; February 2023 is issue date. Routine December 10, 2022 corrected-and-typeset metadata is not an identified error disclosure.

verification_scope: Independent reading of assessment, relevant response, and cited primary publication metadata; original code was not independently rerun.
original_title: Sorting or Steering: The Effects of Housing Discrimination on Neighborhood Choice
materiality_scope: Neighborhood-steering secondary result substantially weakens; overall discrimination conclusion survives.
error: City misspellings and capitalization inconsistencies create erroneous separate city fixed effects.
affected_claim: Minority homebuyers are steered away from high-income white neighborhoods.
corrected_direction: City-only correction attenuates binary minority effect and especially category-specific Black and Asian estimates.
evidence_locator: DP108 PDF p. 9; DP109 response PDF pp. 5–8.
public_date_evidence: I4R series issue March 2024; internal November 22, 2023 manuscript date does not establish public availability.
cohort_recommendation: Eligible for material secondary-error stratum, subject to citation-window rules. Only one complete calendar year (2023) lies strictly between online publication and disclosure.
limitations: Changing treatment of the other-race category and clustering level are contested analytical choices; numerical contrasts here isolate acknowledged city-string error.

verification_scope: Independent reading of assessment, relevant response, and cited primary publication metadata; original code was not independently rerun.
original_title: Major Reforms in Electricity Pricing: Evidence from a Quasi-Experiment
materiality_scope: Two IV robustness specifications lose precision; main OLS result remains. Other omitted-quarter-control corrections strengthen estimates.
error: Some IV code omits stated household clustering, and other IV specifications omit stated quarter fixed effects.
affected_claim: IV robustness support for electricity-pricing reform effects.
corrected_direction: Clustering leaves coefficients unchanged but raises p-values; quarter-FE correction increases absolute effects.
evidence_locator: Report PDF p. 5 and Tables 2–3 PDF p. 10. Table brackets explicitly contain p-values, not standard errors.
public_date_evidence: Internal February 15, 2024 report date and February 28, 2024 OSF upload do not independently establish when the project/file became public.
cohort_recommendation: Retain secondary error claim; event date unresolved, so not presently analysis-eligible.

verification_scope: Independent reading of assessment, relevant response, and cited primary publication metadata; original code was not independently rerun.
original_title: Narrative Identity, Traits, and Trajectories of Depression and Well-Being: A 9-Year Longitudinal Study
materiality_scope: Authors acknowledge one incorrect discussion sentence; numerical models reproduce and broader alleged interpretation errors remain disputed.
error: Discussion sentence incorrectly claims motivation fulfillment improves both well-being and depression over time.
affected_claim: Specific longitudinal interpretation in the discussion.
corrected_direction: Remove unsupported broad claim; no numerical correction documented.
evidence_locator: Authors_response.pdf, PDF p. 2; compare report final version.
public_date_evidence: OSF July 14, 2026 upload timestamps do not establish first public disclosure.
cohort_recommendation: Interpretation-error inventory; materiality and event date insufficient for strict main cohort.

original_title: Religious Festivals and Economic Development: Evidence from the Timing of Mexican Saint Day Festivals
materiality_scope: Primary income effect substantially attenuates; signs and overall conclusions retained, with development-index effect changing less.
error: Missing income sentinel values 99999998/99999999 entered municipality means, and eight December-to-January harvest/festival overlaps were miscoded.
affected_claim: Magnitude of long-run income loss associated with agriculturally coinciding festivals.
corrected_direction: Attenuation of income and development-index effects without sign reversal.
evidence_locator: Matching OSF report file 6602ddb1d9031c00ef03a99b PDF pp. 4 and 9–10; DP124 PDF pp. 6 and 17; author corrigendum PDF pp. 3–5.
public_date_evidence: DP124 publicly issued May 2024 explicitly identifies both coding errors on PDF p. 6. OSF report internally dated March 25, 2024, but upload/internal date alone does not establish earlier public disclosure.
formal_correction_date_evidence: AEA original article landing page labels corrigendum posted on 1/16/2026; long author version internally dated January 15.
verification_scope: Report and author acknowledgement independently read; original code not rerun.
cohort_recommendation: Verified consequential coding error, subject to short prepublication citation history. Do not equate authors disputed robustness/data-collection critiques with these admitted bugs.

original_title: Raising Health Awareness in Rural Communities: A Randomized Experiment in Bangladesh and India
affected_claim: Bangladesh health-information effects identify a newly randomized intervention.
consequence: 5840 matched observations retain exact treatment assignments from two prior interventions. The health-information contrast is bundled with prior treatment histories and cannot isolate the new intervention as claimed.
error_verification: Matched participant IDs, age and income plus exact inherited assignment mapping; report PDF7–9 Table1. Other baseline-date/age inconsistencies PDF13–14 are separate.
date_caveat: IZA explicitly issues the critique March2025. DP cover February2025 and OSF timestamps do not independently establish earlier public release; this is earliest substantiated public evidence found, not proof no earlier warning existed.
limitations: Independent reading of evidence, not rerun of matching code. Do not attribute a numeric treatment-effect correction or intentional misconduct.

original_title: Food insecurity and mental health of women during COVID-19: Evidence from a developing country
affected_claim: Food insecurity worsened between waves and is positively associated with perceived stress as reported.
consequence: Stress items4,5,7,8 were not reverse-coded; food-insecurity wave labels were swapped. Correctly scored models do not support the central stress association as reported. Some categorical contrasts remain positive.
error_verification: Report PDF5–9 shows scoring reconstruction and corrected regressions; 2026 publisher retraction independently confirms scale error and swapped wave labels and says central conclusion unsupported.
additional_public_date_evidence: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0349829 cites the OSF critique as accessed23April2025; retraction itself published21May2026.
date_caveat: Earliest substantiated month found; earlier cover/OSF dates not validated as publicity.
limitations: Original analysis code unavailable. Uncorrected negative coefficients are not the correctly scored result. Observational article does not claim randomized food insecurity.

original_title: Parent–teacher meetings and student outcomes: Evidence from a developing country
affected_claim: School-level randomized parent–teacher meetings identify effects on student outcomes.
consequence: Schools are assigned identically within all nine unions, at odds with described selection of40of76schools; cross-file school identifiers and treatment assignments also conflict. These documented inconsistencies undermine the randomized-design interpretation.
error_verification: Report PDF9,13–14 and conclusionPDF28; subsequently published comment DOI10.1016/j.euroecorev.2025.105021.
date_caveat: Published comment explicitly says available online3April2025. Earlier I4R/IZA month-level circulation may precede this; exact earliest release unresolved within2025. Do not use manuscript received date as exposure.
limitations: A highly improbable assignment pattern is not logically impossible; do not infer fraud. No independent code rerun.

original_title: Acquiescence Bias Inflates Estimates of Conspiratorial Beliefs and Political Misperceptions
affected_claim: Education moderates positive-key responses in the reported direction.
consequence: Fourteen education entries−3105 were treated as continuous values. Dropping or recoding these invalid entries changes the education×positive-key coefficient from negative to positive. The principal wording/acquiescence result remains.
error_verification: Report PDF2–4 and formal corrigendum DOI10.1017/pan.2024.27 acknowledge invalid education coding. Consequence is a secondary substantive direction reversal, not a reversal of the headline.
date_caveat: Publisher explicitly says online24January2025. Cached replication cover says9August2024 but public release on that date is unverified. Eventyear may be2024if independent archived/public announcement evidence emerges; hold earliest-year uncertainty explicit.
limitations: Eligibility depends on prespecified inclusion of substantive secondary-claim errors. Do not advertise as refutation of central acquiescence finding; unresolved earlier exposure prevents treating2025as proven first year.

original_title: Gender Bias in Parental Attitude: An Experimental Approach
affected_claim: Random assignment supports cross-treatment comparisons of parental gender bias
substantive_consequence: Nonrandom allocation contradicts household randomization and removes experimental identification for cross-arm hypotheses. No demonstrated reversal of overall gender-bias result.
evidence: Treatment allocation inherited from nonrandomized Islam study, contradicting reported randomassignment. Replicators match followup dataset to inherited assignment; two hypotheses comparing allocation treatments lose claimed experimental identification.
public_date_evidence: Public I4R report and December 5, 2025 journal commentary; dp214 already discusses reused allocation in 2025, so exact first day unresolved.
limitations: Underlying 2018 raw data unavailable; inference uses overlapping follow-up data. Directly verifies unrestricted arms; restricted-arm assignment less directly observed. Author dispute retained.

original_title: Disloyal Managers and Shareholder Wealth
affected_claim: Corporate opportunity waiver laws reduce firm innovation
substantive_consequence: Figure 1 interactions absorb the intended event-time variation; remaining variation comes from calendar/fiscal-year mismatch. Corrected reanalysis does not show the claimed innovation drop.
evidence: Figure1 implemented treatment interacted with state-year and industry-year fixed effects, absorbing intended treatment variation; residual identification relies on calendar versus fiscal year mismatch. Corrected stacked specification removes innovation decline. Original sample unavailable; authors dispute substantive consequences and document database-version differences.
evidence_locator: PDF pp.6–7,16–17; author response dp286 pp.4–6
public_date_evidence: SSRN public posting July 30, 2025; author-hosted July 21, 2025 version already documents exact FE and time-indexing errors (https://www.haraldhau.com/wp-content/uploads/GHL_Full-Text.pdf PDF pp.3,14).
limitations: Original analysis sample unavailable. Database revisions and sample changes mean all numerical differences cannot be attributed solely to fixing the code. Author response disputes implications; materiality verified narrowly for Figure 1 identification.

original_title: The Effect of High-Tech Clusters on the Productivity of Top Inventors
affected_claim: IV and event-study evidence for causal cluster-size effects on inventor productivity
substantive_consequence: Instrument first differences mix cities; within-city correction reduces first-stage F from 22–39 to 4–7 and markedly widens IV uncertainty. Missing time-zero interaction creates an event-study discontinuity that disappears after correction. Baseline positive association remains.
evidence: Instrument first differences computed across cities because sorting omits city; corrected within-city IV first-stage F falls from22–39 to4–7 and main IV estimates lose precision. Eventtime-zero coefficient uses un-interacted cluster size instead of interaction; correcting removes discontinuity.
public_date_evidence: Dated primary-author blog explicitly documents both coding errors on January 22, 2024. Archived November 16, 2023 PDF exists but writing date alone is not verified public posting.
limitations: Do not equate loss of IV precision with zero effect or assume corrected point estimates all decrease. Earlier public exposure in 2023 remains possible.

original_title: The Welfare Magnet Hypothesis: Evidence from an Immigrant Welfare Scheme in Denmark
affected_claim: Migration response to welfare benefits
substantive_consequence: Stock changes among immigrants aged 30+ conflate migration with residents aging into the group and deaths. Measuring inflows minus outflows reduces the average detrended 2002–2011 decline from about 3,900 to 1,900 people.
evidence: Change in stock of immigrants aged30+ interpreted as net migration but includes existing residents turning30. Comparing actual inflows minus outflows reduces detrended net-flow decline from3900 to1900; separate alternative estimators yield much lower elasticities.
public_date_evidence: Public author thread retrieved via Bluesky public API records June 18, 2025, 11:24:07 UTC. Specific post explains aging into age-30 stock and inflated net-flow differences; next post explains pretrend distortion. Author PDF committed same day: https://github.com/JopieAdema/JopieAdema.github.io/commit/c0335813741a8a74db7265624f27ef6736257588
limitations: The 1.3 versus 0.28 elasticity comparison changes estimands and models and is not a pure error correction. Residence-based flow data differ from original origin-based stocks; report checks correspondence. March 2025 seminar could be earlier exposure, but title alone does not verify specific disclosed content.

original_title: The CRAVE and ARGE scales for motivation states for physical activity and sedentarism: Brazilian Portuguese translation and single-item versions
affected_claim: Representative Brazilian normative scale validation from1168 participants
substantive_consequence: Brazilian data duplicate nearly half the nominal 1,168 rows. After all cleaning, authors identify 541 valid participants and withdraw the claim that the data provide Brazilian normative values.
evidence: 584 response rows repeat as second half of1168-row dataset; authors acknowledge sample handling errors and withdraw normative-data claim. Authors report journal retraction decisionJuly1,2026 and approve it.
evidence_locator: dp313 PDF pp.4–5; dp314 PDF p.5; retraction notice
public_date_evidence: Formal public retraction July 30, 2026 confirms handling errors and withdrawal of normative-data claim. Earlier 2026 I4R exposure may precede this date; private March complaint, April receipt and July decision are not public dates.
limitations: Do not call the valid sample 584: that counts unique half-rows before other exclusions. Main psychometric patterns may persist. Retraction is a later event; exact earliest public day remains unresolved.

original_title: Validation of the CRAVE-C scale in Chinese adults: a four-study examination of competing motivations for physical activity versus rest
affected_claim: Chronic-illness and psychiatric differences in motivations for activity and rest
substantive_consequence: Study 1 contains repeated sessions; Study 2 control sample differs from reported N and some clinical scores exceed the stated scale. Correcting the psychiatric Move comparison reverses its abstract direction; harmonizing coding removes the chronic-illness Rest difference. Draft response withdraws chronic-illness inference because provenance remains unresolved.
evidence: Duplicate control rows and mismatched scoring/sample counts; draft correction withdraws chronic-illness inference and corrects direction of psychiatric Move comparison. Multiple unrecoverable participant links limit other studies.
evidence_locator: dp324 PDF pp.4–5; dp325 PDF pp.4–5,26
public_date_evidence: Public I4R discussion paper in 2026; earliest day not established. dp325 is a coauthor-review draft dated August 25, 2026, not an approved correction.
limitations: The proposed correction explicitly says NOT FOR JOURNAL SUBMISSION and contains blank coauthor approval checkboxes. Do not code a formal published correction or universal author agreement; retain unresolved provenance and recent exposure.

original_title: Banning the purchase of sex increases cases of rape: evidence from Sweden
affected_claim: Swedish sex-purchase ban increased reported rape by44–62 percent
substantive_consequence: Treatment dummy is collinear with year fixed effects; Stata regressor order produces the reported coefficient after dropping other terms. The purported RDD effect therefore is not identified by the stated specification. Further bandwidth and implementation errors affect alternatives.
evidence: Treatment-year dummy is collinear with year fixed effects. Stata retains it only by dropping other regressors; variable ordering changes result. Bandwidth for bias estimation used instead of stated treatment-effect bandwidth. Corrected estimates shrink sharply; standard model cannot estimate stated coefficient.
public_date_evidence: dp226 PDF p.4 explicitly recounts posting the March 2024 critique online after contacting author/editor; archived report supports 2024 disclosure. Later editor note and retraction in 2025 do not reset clock.
limitations: Separate literal errors from revised seasonal models and disputed sample changes. Later retraction DOI 10.1007/s00148-025-01114-2 should be retained as a separate event.

original_title: Temperature and Decisions: Evidence from207,000 Court Cases
affected_claim: Warmer days reduce judges granting asylum
substantive_consequence: Weather-location/time matching errors and coding withdrawn applications as judicial denials reduce the estimated temperature effect by roughly two-thirds after correction. Expanding sample years is a separate extension.
evidence: Wrong time zone/weather averaging, wrong geographical court-weather matches, and withdrawn applications counted as judicial rejections. Correction reduces original estimate about two-thirds; reply restores finding using changed Chinese-applicant exclusion. Separate reanalysis/extending sample not conflated with error correction.
public_date_evidence: SSRN says Posted August 5, 2020 and abstract already documents coding/data errors and two-thirds reduction; Harvard Discussion Paper 1036 archived July 7, 2020 manuscript.
limitations: Public 2020 date precedes 2022 journal comment. Reply obtains a restored effect after additionally excluding Chinese applicants; do not attribute that changed sample to correction alone.

original_title: Development Effects of Electrification: Evidence from the Topographic Placement of Hydropower Plants in Brazil
affected_claim: Electrification increases HDI and housing values in Brazil
substantive_consequence: IV simulation and estimation use inconsistent Amazon definitions. Additional code omits HDI definition harmonization and includes populations with missing outcomes in aggregation denominators, implicitly treating missing outcomes as zero; correcting these markedly reduces HDI effects.
evidence: Amazon boundary inconsistent between IV simulation and estimation; acknowledged earlier2021 correction. Additional errors omit HDI definition adjustment and include populations of missing-outcome municipalities in denominator, treating missing outcomes as zero; correcting lowers HDI effects substantially.
public_date_evidence: SSRN USAEE Working Paper 21-529 states Posted December 10, 2021. Abstract explicitly says inconsistent Amazon demarcations and loss of precision after consistent implementation. Later HDI/aggregation errors are additional disclosures, not necessarily already in this version.
limitations: Earliest material error at article level established in 2021 for inconsistent Amazon definition. Do not date every later HDI/aggregation error to 2021. Random-seed instability is a separate robustness issue; exact first public day may precede SSRN posting.
